A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the absence of a yield criterion and with the no-slope assumption, the final slump shape is determined by the initial geometry of the dam, the volume and the initial height of the fluid.
the volume-of-fluid method, when coupled with either the regularized viscosity or the augmented-Lagrangia scheme, is an accurate and efficient tool for simulating the collapse of a viscoplastic dam.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the collapse and slump are dominated by the inertia of the fluid, and that the final shape is controlled by a balance between inertia and the resistance to deformation provided by the fluid’s viscosity.
the collapse and slump of viscoplastic fluids are governed by the same mechanisms as those of Newtonian fluids, and that the main difference is that the former are more prone to failure.
the final slump shape is insensitive to the mode of initial collapse, provided that the initial collapse is not too rapid.
